slot.brief: Excess pressure in soap bubbles: two soap bubbles of different radii in contact or compared; use 4T/r (or 2T/r distinction between a bubble and a drop) to find a ratio of excess pressures.

stem: Two soap bubbles have radii $2$ mm and $3$ mm. What is the ratio of the excess pressure in the smaller bubble to that in the larger bubble?

verdicts.working: For a soap bubble, excess pressure is $4T/r$. Thus the ratio is $(4T/2)/(4T/3)=3/2$.

working:
For a soap bubble, $\Delta P=\dfrac{4T}{r}$.
$\dfrac{\Delta P_{2\,\text{mm}}}{\Delta P_{3\,\text{mm}}}=\dfrac{3}{2}$

Independent check: For a soap bubble, excess pressure is $4T/r$. Thus the ratio is $(4T/2)/(4T/3)=3/2$.
solution:
For a soap bubble, the excess pressure is $\Delta P=\dfrac{4T}{r}$. Hence,
$$\frac{\Delta P_{2\,\text{mm}}}{\Delta P_{3\,\text{mm}}}=\frac{4T/2}{4T/3}=\boxed{\dfrac{3}{2}}$$
